chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements [that have been place]d in the Flesh.
chapter_note: The chapter opens with a clear hagiographic dialogue frame (¶1), then shifts into impersonal, systematic exposition about the four light elements, their mixture with Darkness, and their purification in the body (¶2–8). The closing paragraph (¶9) applies the process to the elect/sinners and introduces institutional/ethical categories and transmigration in a hortatory register; this looks like later pastoral application rather than the older cosmological mechanism itself. No NT citation overlay is present.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic opening: 'Once again… the apostle… congregation. He speaks thus:' is compilation frame and must not be in core.

paragraphs.core_text: The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [ ... ] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the Darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [ ... ] and become a danger to the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanics: primordial 'first struggle', mixture with Darkness/enemy, descent into body, stripping polluted garments—system description rather than institutional instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered/chain-style correspondential mapping (element → bodily substance → emotion → bodily state) in expository voice; no frame or church categories.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.240⟩
Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same systematic chain mapping for another element; manuscript page marker preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Same old-teaching style: element/process language ('disgorge') + triadic chain.

paragraphs.core_text: The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though 'tree' is obscure/corrupt, the syntax remains within the same mechanical emission-chain; no institutional register. Likely part of the original fourfold schema, albeit fragmentary.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission of the [tear] is the [ ... ] of these twelve emissions.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative line referring to a counted set ('these twelve emissions'), characteristic of the systematic teaching layer even though fragmentary.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] these four elements shall [ ... ] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [ ... ] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-description of purification via 'soul food' entering the body, re-establishment in 'living image'/'new man', ascent/rest—cosmological soteriology stated as mechanism, not rule.

Institutional application and moral categorization: 'the elect' vs 'sinners' as the hinge for purification; exhortative/administrative register rather than impersonal mechanism. Even if based on core doctrine, this paragraph reads as later community application.
